in the set of squares and divisors in a short intervalThanks: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 42A05, 11A05Thanks: Keywords and phrases: squares, trigonometric polynomials, divisorsThanks: ORCID: 0000-0001-8774-8334
Mikhail R. Gabdullin
Address: Department of mathematics, 1409 West Green Street, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Urbana, IL 61801, USA; Steklov Mathematical Institute,
Gubkina str., 8, Moscow, 119991, Russia
Email address: gabdullin.mikhail@yandex.ru, mikhailg@illinois.edu
Date: August 24, 2026
Abstract.
Let γ0=5−12=0.618​… . We prove that, for any ε>0 and any trigonometric polynomial f with frequencies in the set {n2:N⩽n⩽N+Nγ0−ε}, the inequality
∥f∥4≪ε−1/4∥f∥2
holds, which makes a progress on a conjecture of Cilleruelo and Córdoba. We also present a connection between this conjecture and the conjecture of Ruzsa which asserts that, for any ε>0, there is C⁡(ε)>0 such that each positive integer N has at most C⁡(ε) divisors in the interval [N1/2,N1/2+N1/2−ε].
1. Introduction
Let us say that a trigonometric polynomial f has frequencies in a set A⊆ℤ if f⁡(x)=∑n∈Aan​e​(n​x) with an∈ℂ (here and in what follows e⁡(x)=e2​π​i​x). Let p>2. Recall that a set A⊆ℤ is said to be a Λp-set if there exists a constant C⁡(A,p)>0 such that for any trigonometric polynomial f with frequencies in the set A, the inequality
(1.1)
‖f‖p⩽C⁡(A,p)​‖f‖2
holds, where ‖f‖p=(∫𝕋|f⁡(x)|p​𝑑x)1/p and 𝕋=ℝ/ℤ. It is easy to show that if a set A is a Λp-set for some p>2, then the counting function of A cannot grow too fast. To be more precise, let AN=A∩[−N,N] and f⁡(x)=∑n∈ANe⁡(n​x); then by the properties of the Dirichlet kernel DN​(x)=∑|k|⩽Ne⁡(k​x), Hölder’s inequality and (1.1),
|AN|=f⁡(0)=(f∗DN)​(0)=∫𝕋f⁡(−y)​DN​(y)​𝑑y⩽‖f‖p​‖DN‖q≪|AN|1/2​N1/p
(here q is defined by 1/p+1/q=1), and, hence, |AN|≪N2/p. Using probabilistic methods, Bourgain [1] showed that this upper bound is tight: for instance, Theorem 3 in [1] states that for any p>2, there exists a Λp-subset A of the set of prime numbers of maximal density, that is, with lim¯N→∞|AN|N−2/p≫1. However, that proof does not produce any examples of Λp-sets. On the other hand, we note that there is the classical result that any lacunary sequence is a Λp-set for every p>2 (e.g., [7], Theorem 3.6.4).
In this regard, it is of a great interest to find polynomial sequences which are Λp-sets. There is a famous and still unsolved conjecture about the set of squares {n2:n∈ℕ}, which was discussed by W. Rudin (see the end of section 4.6 in [11]).
Conjecture 1.1.
The set of squares is a Λp-set for any 2<p<4.
